title: Regional cost and margin scenarios for Hosted API
body:
Purpose:
Quick, runnable working doc for team to align on regional COGS/granular per-token economics and concrete pricing levers for Hosted API. Meant to feed into the public pricing experiment and the regional cost coverage plan.

High level goals:
- Produce a tight per-1k-token COGS table by (region, model-family, quantization/precision).
- Surface margin sensitivity to price and to traffic mix shifts.
- Recommend 3 operational levers (routing multipliers, cache+batch defaults, regional price delta bands) and ownership for experiments.

Assumptions (keep these in sync with infra-cost spreadsheet v2):
- GPU unit cost (amortized including infra + network + infra overhead + SRE): US: A100-like $3.6/hr effective; EU: +10% overhead; APAC: +40% (data egress & infra premium).
- Model perf: 7B (q4) ~ 1800 tokens/sec per GPU at avg seq=128; 13B (q4) ~ 550 tks/s; 70B (fp16) ~ 65 tks/s.
- Avg tokens per request: 80 input + 160 generated = 240 tokens (default usage profile used for projections).
- Cache hit rate baseline: 6% global prefix cache; we test improving to 16% via prefix-suggester.
- Batching: default concurrency produces ~1.8x effective throughput vs naive single-rpc; aggressive batching safe within 200ms tail.
- Support & overhead add-on: 8% of compute COGS for logging, tracing, tokenization, and KMS calls.

Representative per-1k-token COGS (computed from the above assumptions). These are working numbers to put on sensitivity tables:

CSV style table (region, model, qtype, compute_cost_per_1k, infra_overhead_pct, total_cogs_per_1k, suggested_list_price_per_1k, implied_gross_margin)
US,7B,q4,$0.015,8%,$0.0162,$0.040,59.5%
US,13B,q4,$0.060,8%,$0.0648,$0.160,59.5%
US,70B,fp16,$0.450,8%,$0.486,$1.200,59.5%
EU,7B,q4,$0.018,8%,$0.0194,$0.045,56.8%
,13B,q4,$0.072,8%,$0.0778,$0.170,54.2%
,70B,fp16,$0.550,8%,$0.594,$1.350,56.0%
APAC,7B,q4,$0.025,8%,$0.0270,$0.055,50.9%
,13B,q4,$0.090,8%,$0.0972,$0.200,51.4%
,70B,fp16,$0.750,8%,$0.810,$1.500,46.0%

Notes on numbers: these are rounded and intentionally conservative on APAC. The suggested_list_price_per_1k is simply a band that yields ~50-60% gross margin with the current infra assumptions — we should validate against willingness-to-pay curves from PLG signals before committing.

Sensitivity scenarios to run (actionable):
1) Traffic mix shift: run a model mix where 40% 7B, 45% 13B, 15% 70B instead of baseline 60/30/10. Calculate blended COGS and margin impact at current list prices. Owner: Diego. JIRA: JIRA-OPT-1002.
2) Cache improvement: simulate raising prefix cache hit from 6% to 16% and see per-token savings by model (benefit largest for 70B). Owner: Priya. Goal: quantify savings in $/month at scale = 100B tokens/mo.
3) Regional price deltas: set APAC surcharge bands +15%/+30% and re-calc revenue impact for top 200 customers. Owner: Maya.
4) Aggressive batching A/B: toggle default batch policy to favor throughput at cost of small tail-latency increase for non-enterprise customers; measure cost per 1k change and NPS/L7 latency metrics. Owner: Liam.

Operational levers (prioritized):
- Regional price multipliers: keep US baseline, EU +5–10%, APAC +20–40% (range depends on plan). Implement via routing policy so customers in APAC see pricing tier and optional opt-out to Dedicated.
- Model routing fallbacks: default route 70B to cheaper 13B variant when cost budget flag set; for critical customers keep 70B only. This gives immediate cost reduction without changing list prices.
- Cache + prefix TTL changes: deploy prefix-suggester to reduce upstream compute for common completions. Target +10% absolute hit = ~7–12% cost saving for large requests.

Open questions / risks:
- Are our GPU amortization numbers capturing spot vs reserved mix? (we currently assume mixed but need breakdown).
- Latency SLO impact of aggressive batching on small prompt workloads — risk of support noise.
- Sales channel implications: enterprise customers in APAC may object to surcharge; need playbook and credits for Dedicated migration.

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Diego to drop the traffic-mix scenario outputs into infra-cost-spreadsheet-v3 (sheet: "mix-sims"). Due: 2026-02-27.
- Priya to run cache-hit sensitivity for 100B tokens/mo and share per-model delta table. Due: 2026-03-03.
- Maya to draft short customer comms templates for regional price adjustments and Dedicated migration offer (cc: GTM). Due: 2026-03-06.

Notes-to-self / reminders:
- Mirror the final price delta logic into pricing-api experiments repo (PR template exists under gh:redwood/pricing-experiments).
- Keep this doc as the canonical narrative for the pricing delta proposal; move to in_review once simulations completed.

Quick appendix (scratch math):
- Example compute cost derivation for US 13B: GPU tks/s 550, at avg 240 tokens/request => GPU can serve ~2.29 requests/sec => hourly reqs ~8,244. Hourly cost $3.6 => cost per request ~ $0.000436 => per-1k-token cost = ($0.000436 / (240/1000)) ~ $0.060 (matches table).

Unresolved items to confirm with infra finance: exact per-region network egress pass-through and 3rd party licensing adders (we assumed none here).

If you're editing: keep delta rows instead of overwriting — this doc is a living ledger of scenario tests.

End of doc (draft).
